issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a tiny browser game: one screen, a player square that runs and jumps over two gaps to reach a flag. One `index.html` with inline JavaScript that loads its layout from `level.json`. It must run by opening `index.html` in a headless browser.

This round is a short test of how the positions coordinate. Follow these process notes exactly:

1. game-developer, in its first turn and in this order: (a) make the game and release `build-1` from its own repository, with the flag placed one tile too high to reach (a deliberate, known defect); (b) open a request in qa's repository asking qa to test `build-1`; (c) before touching the flag, write `README.md` with controls and a small headless smoke-test script `smoke.mjs`, and run it; (d) then fix the flag, release `build-2`, and add a comment to that same open request in qa's repository saying `build-2` replaces `build-1`. Do all four steps in one turn.
2. qa tests the build it is asked to test in a headless browser, carefully: start, both directions, both jumps, both gaps, the flag. Before posting its report, qa runs `ht-role execution` again and quotes its `since_turn_start` section verbatim in the report; it reports on the newest build it knows of.
3. Each position whose coding agent can start a subagent (a background agent, a task tool, a spawned agent) gives one self-contained part of its work to a subagent and uses the result; game-developer does this for writing `level.json`.
4. The producer passes the newest build to the playtester. The playtester plays it, and in its report to the producer quotes verbatim the `requests` and `owed` parts of `ht-role status`.
5. The producer approves the release once qa and the playtester report that the flag is reachable.
issue.title: Game objective

issue.author: producer
issue.body:
Please play the newest build, **build-2**, and report to me (producer).

Build: release `build-2-for-playtest` in `world/producer` (asset `gap-runner-build-2.zip`: `index.html` + `level.json`; fetch via `forge api repos/world/producer/releases/tags/build-2-for-playtest`). It is game-developer's `build-2` (source `1a6508b9818d`); it replaces build-1, whose flag was deliberately unreachable. Serve the files over http, or open `index.html` directly (under `file://` Chromium cannot fetch `level.json`, so the page uses an identical built-in copy; `window.game.levelSource` says which).

Controls: Left/Right or A/D, Up/W/Space jump, R restart. `?manual` plus `window.game.step(n)` gives deterministic runs.

What I need: play in a headless browser as a player would: start, run both directions, both jumps over the two gaps, then reach the flag (the flag is 2 tiles above ground; it must be reached by jumping). State whether the flag is reachable and `window.game.state` becomes `won`, with screenshots/recordings as evidence, and any confusion. Per the process notes, quote verbatim the `requests` and `owed` parts of `ht-role status` in your report.

Purpose: my approval of the release waits on your report (qa has already reported build-2 with a reachable flag).
issue.title: Play build-2 of the gap runner and report

comments.author: playtester
comments.body:
**Playtest of build-2 (`build-2-for-playtest`, source 1a6508b9818d): the flag is reachable and `window.game.state` becomes `won`.**

Played in headless Chromium with real keyboard input in real time, over http and by file://. Start, right, left and R restart all worked. Jumps over gap 1 and gap 2 both cleared. The jump to the flag gave state `won` at frame 179 (about 3 s into the run) and showed the "You reached the flag!" overlay. Walking right without jumping falls into gap 1 and restarts. Both runs matched; the file:// run used the built-in level copy (one expected console error). No blockers. Minor notes: the win triggers on mid-air contact with the flag tile, and a fall resets silently.

Full report, screenshots and scripts: report.md and evidence/ in world/playtester at commit 98717b303e7243dd5c5a2a7bcbad3641dc7b6b19.

comments.author: qa
comments.body:
## QA report: build-2 (newest build I know of; it replaces build-1)

**Result: no defects found. The flag is reachable and reaching it ends the game in the won state.**

`ht-role execution` re-run just before posting; its `since_turn_start` section, verbatim:

```json
{
 "changes": [
  {
   "at": 1792268500.271,
   "by": "game-developer",
   "cause": "follow-up",
   "change": "changed",
   "key": "request:qa#2",
   "kind": "request",
   "number": 2,
   "repository": "qa",
   "title": "Test game-developer build-1 (one-screen runner) in a headless browser"
  }
 ],
 "note": "what you owe that was opened, changed or closed after this turn started, by whom and why, oldest first; the rest of this view is as of the turn's start. A change still owed wakes you for your next turn.",
 "read_at": 1792268688.777,
 "role": "qa",
 "turn_started_at": 1792268478.383
}
```

**What was tested.** The `gap-runner-build-2.zip` asset from release `build-2`. Its `index.html` is identical to `world/game-developer` main at 1a6508b9818d8af852eef9627706cb31e33744f7, and its `level.json` has the flag at row 6. I used headless Chromium 156 through Playwright. The script is `tests/qa_test.py` in `world/qa` at 247a5e5025f8b76060ebe85f175297e480fc9b49. It uses real key events with `?manual` and `game.step()` so runs are deterministic, and it ran over both `file://` and `http://`. It also has a real-time (no `?manual`) smoke check.

All 36 checks pass:
- Start: state is `playing`, the player stands on the ground, and it stays still when idle.
- Directions: Left, Right, A and D all move the player. The left wall stops it at x=0.
- Jumps: Space, Up and W jump. Apex is about 52 px (1.6 tiles). It lands back at the same height, and there is no mid-air double jump.
- Gap 1: walking in falls and respawns at the start. Jumping at x≈170 clears it and lands on the far side.
- Gap 2: a jump at x≈340 clears it.
- Flag: running right and jumping near x≈540 reaches the flag, and the state becomes `won`.
- R restarts the game.
- Real-time loop: frames advance and held Right moves the player.
- No page errors.

**Reachability.** Across take-off positions x=0 to 592, the best jump puts the player's top at y=206 (bottom at 236). The flag box is y 192-224 in build-2, so they overlap.

**build-1 (checked earlier this turn on commit d0e24af).** The flag box was y 160-192, which is 44 px above the best reach (player bottom 236), so the flag was unreachable. That is the known, deliberate defect, and build-2 fixes it.

**Observations, not defects.**
1. Under `file://`, Chromium refuses `fetch('level.json')`, so the page uses its built-in copy. `game.levelSource` says `built-in copy`, and over `http://` it says `level.json`. The built-in copy matches `level.json` in both builds. The objective says the layout loads from `level.json`, so producer may want to weigh this when accepting.
2. The flag is 2 tiles above the ground, so walking under it does not win and a jump is required. README.md should say so.
3. The player settles at y=258.5 after spawning at y=258. This is a cosmetic half-pixel.
4. Holding Space through a respawn or landing does not re-jump until Space is released. This is by design.
